original: AS AMENDED a bill for an ordinance amending Title 27 of the Revised Municipal Code of the City and County of Denver to revise definitions and procedures set forth therein for greater clarity and to extend the minimum affordability period for properties that receive city subsidies from twenty years to sixty years. Amends Section 27 of the Denver Revised Municipal Code (DRMC) to approve revisions to the Affordable Housing Preservation ordinance including definitions and procedures intended to clarify applicability to income-restricted properties within the city and extension of the minimum period of affordability from 20 years to 60 years. sampled: Council Bill 18-1089, presented by Laura Brzezinski of the Office of Economic Development and reviewed by the Safety Committee, proposes increasing the minimum affordability period for city-subsidized housing projects from 20 years to 60 years, with an amendment introduced by Councilwoman Kenny limiting the change to contracts dated on or after February 1, 2019, to provide certainty for developers whose tax credit letters of intent to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority are due before that deadline. sampled: The City Council of Long Beach is contemplating a strategic move to enter the energy market, with a potential annual power purchase estimated at $150 million. Additionally, concerns have been raised regarding public engagement and awareness in the decision-making process of the energy program, alongside the identification of key risks and uncertainties associated with transitioning to a new energy model.

original: Recommendation to request City Manager to work with the Department of Development Services to evaluate the feasibility of establishing, in accordance with state and federal auditing requirements, a single Emergency Rental Assistance application for landlords with multiple tenants in communities at elevated risk of eviction. This funding would cover past rental arrears and up to three months of future rental obligation for eligible tenants. Participation in this program should allow tenants whose rental debt was covered an additional 90 days of protection from eviction past the final date of payment of back rent, and Direct the Department of Development Services to publicize data regarding the rental assistance program on a public dashboard.
sampled: Recommendation by Vice Mayor Richardson, co-sponsored by Councilwomen Zendaya and Allen, directing the City Manager and Department of Development Services to evaluate a streamlined single emergency rental assistance application for landlords with multiple tenants in high-eviction-risk communities, and to publish program data on a public dashboard. Long Beach has disbursed $64 million of its $250 million Recovery Act allocation, assisting approximately 2,500 households, while 15,800 households remain behind on rent and at risk of eviction, with an estimated 43,000 residents and 16,000 children affected. Application barriers have left 4,500 applications unfilled and 8,500 incomplete. Updated US Treasury guidance permitting advance payments to landlords with reduced proof-of-eligibility requirements supports the feasibility of the proposed single-application model, based on experience with the Carmelita projects.

original: Recommendation to request the following recommendations of the Illegal Explosives and Fireworks Action Plan to address the illegal use of fireworks and explosives in Long Beach: 1) Request City Attorney to draft an ordinance that would include a person who owns, rents, leases or otherwise has possession of a premises as a responsible party for the illegal use, discharge, possession, storage or sale of fireworks on the premises; 2) Request City Attorney and City Manager to report back to the City Council with options for increasing the penalties for anyone cited or arrested for fireworks violations; 3) Request City Attorney and City Manager to report back to the City Council on the feasibility of including an administrative citation process for illegal fireworks use, to allow for additional enforcement capability in Long Beach; 4) Request City Manager to assess the feasibility of establishing an online portal or GoLongBeach app feature for residents to submit video evidence of fireworks violations for referral to the City Prosecutor;
sampled: Recommendation to adopt Item 25, an Illegal Explosives and Fireworks Action Plan for Long Beach comprising 7 requests sponsored by Councilman Austin, Councilwoman Zendejas, Vice Mayor Andrews, and Councilmember Richardson.
